# Plan: Open the universe to contributors

## Sources

`docs/game-design.md` "After the episode". `content/puzzles/service-panel.json` grants `flag:service-panel-open`. `artifactSchema` (`name`, `description`, `requires`, `links`) and `communitySchema` are in `src/content/schema.ts`. `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/swarm-community.yml` is the SwarmOS intake form, so the new forms use the `swarm:community` label. `src/world/archive-view.ts` already prints `FILED BY`.

## In-game

- `content/artifacts/forge.json`: `requires: flag:service-panel-open`. Text is in-world: the network accepts new transmissions from Observers who sign their work, nothing is added without review, and filings go to a real address. `links`: prefilled `https://github.com/supernovae/signal-lost/issues/new?template=propose-transmission.yml` and `...propose-archive-entry.yml`, and the repository itself.
- `src/app/tools.ts`: one generic tool per available artifact, labelled with its `name`. It prints the description and opens `src/world/artifact-view.ts`, a panel of real links with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and `target="_blank"`. Nothing fetches at runtime. No GitHub API calls, no token.
- A locked line: FORGE also says local write is denied, so it is partly accessible by design.
- `TRANSMISSIONS` prints `FILED BY: <author>` when a transmission has attribution, as the archive view does.
- `content/community/first-light.json`: a real community package with a transmission and an archive entry, unlocked by `flag:service-panel-open`, with attribution naming the project maintainers and `provenance` saying it ships as the example. No invented contributors.
- `content/characters/echo.json`: a reaction to reading the community archive entry (it was not written by anyone ECHO remembers), and a reaction to opening FORGE, recorded through a new `grantsOnOpen` field on artifacts (`flag:forge-opened`).
- `content/puzzles/service-panel.json`: the panel's success text now mentions power reaching the terminal, so FORGE's appearance has a cause.

## Repository

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/propose-transmission.yml` and `propose-archive-entry.yml`: forms needing no code, using label `swarm:community`.
- `docs/content-authoring.md`: full worked example of adding a transmission (file path, JSON, unlocking, attribution, `npm run content:validate`, how to see it in game, PR). `docs/swarmos.md` is left for the release WorkUnit.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: ways to contribute with no code (issue forms), with code and no SwarmOS (fork and PR), and with SwarmOS (agent path, pointing at `AGENTS.md`).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/contribution.test.ts`:
  - extracts the worked example's fenced JSON from `docs/content-authoring.md`, writes it to a temporary copy of `content/` at the path the doc gives, runs `node scripts/validate-content.ts`, and asserts success and that the new id is in the loaded content;
  - asserts FORGE's issue links name form files that exist, and that the artifact is locked before the flag;
  - asserts no `token`/`ghp_` strings in `src` or `content` and no `api.github.com`;
  - asserts the community package is loaded with visible attribution data.
- `tests/e2e/forge.spec.ts`: FORGE is absent until the panel opens; opening it shows the links; the community entry shows `FILED BY`.

## Files

New: the above. Changed: `src/app/tools.ts`, `src/content/schema.ts`, `src/content/validate.ts`, `content/characters/echo.json`, `content/puzzles/service-panel.json`, `src/style.css`, `tests/unit/content.test.ts`.

## Out of scope

README, full docs set, and the roadmap (release WorkUnit). Automatic merging or a generated contribution history.

# Test plan

Local commands: `npx vitest run tests/unit/contribution.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts`, `npm run content:validate`, `npm run lint`. Browser evidence comes from the PR's `Browser tests` workflow, which runs `tests/e2e/forge.spec.ts`. Developer and tester may complete with browser evidence pending CI.

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FORGE locked until the discovery, then explains in-world and offers prefilled links | `contribution.test.ts`: artifact unavailable without the flag, links resolve to real form files. `forge.spec.ts`: tool absent, then present with links. | Developer; CI |
| Issue forms for a transmission and an archive entry, no code needed | `contribution.test.ts`: both files exist with the `swarm:community` label and no code fields. Tester reads the forms. | Developer; tester inspects |
| A community package loads as real content with visible attribution | `contribution.test.ts` on loaded content. `forge.spec.ts`: `FILED BY` is shown in game. | Developer; CI |
| `docs/content-authoring.md` worked example, performed by a test against a temporary content set | `contribution.test.ts` extracts and validates the doc's own JSON. Output is captured through a file, because stdio pipes lose data in the validation sandbox. | Developer; tester reuses |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers with and without code, with and without SwarmOS | `contribution.test.ts` asserts the sections and that linked paths exist. Tester reads for accuracy. | Developer; tester inspects |

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs the local commands above.
- **Tester:** independently inspects source, content and documents against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy.

VERDICT: APPROVED

The proposed plan covers the WorkUnit objective, constraints, and all five acceptance criteria. No blocking revisions are required.

| Contract area | Audit and verified evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secret discovery and partly accessible FORGE | `content/puzzles/service-panel.json` grants `flag:service-panel-open` after the optional service puzzle; `docs/game-design.md`, “After the episode,” explicitly connects that discovery to FORGE. The plan gates the artifact on that flag and retains a local-write-denied limitation. Unit and browser checks cover locked/unlocked access. | Covered |
| Links only; no credentials or runtime GitHub API | The proposed artifact contains ordinary repository and issue-form links, rendered as anchors. The plan explicitly excludes runtime fetching and credentials and includes a source scan. | Covered |
| Honest attribution and participation | The shipped example is attributed to project maintainers with explicit example provenance. No invented contributors or participation metrics are proposed. Tester content inspection remains necessary; string scans alone cannot establish honesty. | Covered |
| Two no-code contribution forms | Two named forms under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` are proposed, with existence/label checks and independent usability inspection. The existing `swarm-community.yml` confirms the intake label. Issue templates are outside the protected workflow paths. | Covered |
| Real community content with visible attribution | `src/content/validate.ts` already flattens community transmissions and archives and inherits package attribution. `src/world/archive-view.ts` already renders `FILED BY`; the plan adds transmission credits and a browser assertion for the community archive. | Covered |
| Worked authoring example exercised against temporary content | The test extracts the documentation's JSON, writes it at the documented path in a temporary content copy, validates it, and checks the new loaded ID. `scripts/validate-content.ts` accepts a content-root argument; `src/content/node.ts` supports arbitrary roots. | Covered |
| Contribution routes with/without code and SwarmOS | `CONTRIBUTING.md` will describe issue forms, ordinary fork/PR contribution, and the optional SwarmOS route; section/path checks and tester accuracy review cover the criterion. | Covered |
| Scope, architecture, and protected paths | Content remains declarative, artifact tools generic, and DOM rendering in a world view. Planned changes introduce no dependencies or protected harness edits. ECHO reactions and the service-panel wording directly support the specified discovery experience. | Covered |
| Validation ownership and environment | Focused unit/content/lint checks belong to the developer; tester independently inspects and reuses applicable results; coordinator owns complete trusted-base validation. Browser evidence is deferred to existing CI, consistent with sandbox restrictions. | Covered |

## Implementation handoff

- Keep artifact availability filtering in the app layer using the generic condition evaluator and `game.facts()`. `Game.isAvailable()` currently resolves puzzle IDs only; it cannot be used for artifact IDs. No puzzle-engine change is needed for generic artifact filtering.
- Complete the new `grantsOnOpen` field across schema, reference validation, and the tool action: register artifact grants as flag producers, validate grant references, grant through `game.grant()`, and refresh/reaction handling after opening. The planned schema/validator/content tests should cover this boundary. Existing save persistence is available through `game.grant()`.
- Put unlock requirements on the community transmission and archive themselves: the current community package schema has no package-level `requires`. Existing flattening and attribution inheritance supply the remaining integration.
- The temporary authoring test must pass its temporary content root to the CLI and load that same root for the ID assertion. Existing `tests/unit/content.test.ts` demonstrates file-backed child-process output capture and cleanup.
- Use the existing `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` production-build interception under `/signal-lost/`; do not add a preview server. Browser tests should inspect link destinations rather than depend on reaching GitHub.

## Review evidence and limits

Read `.swarm/active/REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` in full. It repeats the current design and test-plan artifacts; it contains no independent previous verdict or additional unmerged lesson requiring a plan change. Source inspection confirms the factual claims in the plan's Sources section and the file-backed output precedent in the test plan. No implementation tests were run for this plan review. Approval is advisory and does not replace coordinator validation or the required passing browser workflow before merge. The configured plan gate remains `none`.
